questions.question_text: You hear a nurse briefing her colleague about a patient. What does she warn her colleague about?
options: The patient is allergic to some types of antibiotics.
Care must be taken to prevent the patient from falling.
Oxygen may be needed if the patient becomes breathless.

questions.question_text: You hear the manager of a care home for the elderly talking to the nursing staff. He says that errors in dispensing medication to patients usually result from
options: interruptions while calculating dosages.
a failure to check for patients' allergies.
administering drugs late in the day.

questions.question_text: You hear part of a morning briefing on a hospital ward. What is the plan for the patient today?
options: Her emotional state will be carefully observed.
She will be transferred to a more specialised unit.
A social worker will come to see what help she needs.

questions.question_text: You hear part of an ante-natal consultation at a GP practice. What does the patient want to know about?
options: the advisability of a home birth
ways of avoiding post-natal depression
what painkillers might be available during labour

audios.title: You hear a clinician called Jonathan Cross giving a presentation to a group of healthcare providers. You now have 90 seconds to read the questions before the audio starts.

questions.question_text: Jonathan says that when considering a policy of open visiting hours, clinicians are
options: generally opposed to the push for change.
essential to its success or failure.
beginning to see the rationale behind it.

questions.question_text: Jonathan believes that having family present in critical care units
options: will cause disharmony among healthcare professionals.
makes little difference to the treatment given to patients.
is potentially dangerous to both staff and patients.

questions.question_text: Jonathan uses statistical information to show that after visiting hours were opened
options: clinicians experienced higher levels of fatigue.
the attitude of staff remained positive.
nurses felt more of a strain than other staff.

questions.question_text: Jonathan says that the possibility of family burnout is an important issue because
options: it is an area that has yet to be sufficiently studied.
the amount of resources needed to overcome it is too great.
it should be considered alongside the change in visiting hours.

questions.question_text: What does Jonathan say about full family presence during open visiting hours?
options: it provides the family a sense of fulfilment during stressful times.
the benefits clearly outweigh any negative aspects.
there are still times where it may be considered inappropriate.

questions.question_text: Jonathan closes by outlining the facts on open visiting hours in order to
options: rationalise any misconceptions listeners may have.
illustrate that its opponents are mistaken in their views.
give advice to hospitals ready to implement the new policy.
